title: Why One AI Agent Isn’t Enough (And How to Run 1,000) - CJ Avilla & Harrison Stall, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic staff present 'flows' in Claude managed agents: a lead agent self-orchestrates a fan-out of isolated-context sub-agents across phases, with per-session budgets, durable event streams, and credential vaults. The most transferable content is the diagnosis of single-agent failure modes (laziness, self-preferential bias, goal drift) and the Bug Hunter PR-review flow pattern.

takeaways.technique: Sliced fan-out PR review with adversarial verify phase (Bug Hunter)
takeaways.what_they_do: Split the PR diff into slices, give each slice its own isolated-context reviewer agent that lists candidate problems, then a second phase that agrees/disagrees per candidate, then a prover phase that checks out the repo and tries to reproduce/verify each surviving candidate before posting inline comments with severity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it takes your code, splits it up into these slices, each of those slices is handed to an individual context

takeaways.technique: Isolated per-item context to counter agentic laziness and goal drift
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one agent scanning N items (which stops early once things look fine and loses late-prompt constraints during compaction), fan out one dedicated agent per item so coverage is guaranteed and the goal is re-injected per sub-agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: after it sees 35 services are healthy, then it starts to like convince itself that oh, it's like everything looks good

takeaways.technique: Per-phase model tiering and per-session budget caps
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt the orchestrator to assign cheap models to high-volume scan phases and expensive models only to the review/verify phase, and set a hard dollar budget per session that pauses (not discards) work when hit, resumable after top-up.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for the scan phase, we can use Haiku, a really fast, efficient model ... I want to have Fable review all the details
takeaways.numbers: Example budget of $1.25 per flow; budget-reached event pauses and resumes without redoing work

takeaways.what_they_do: Sandboxes only ever see fake placeholder secrets; a real credential is substituted at an egress proxy only for an allowlisted destination domain, and the environment firewall blocks all other egress.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every container that has access to any secret, you just totally fake the secrets ... only on the way out ... do those credentials actually get substituted

takeaways.technique: Durable event stream as the observability substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: Every tool call, message send/receive, and handoff is emitted to a single durable event log per session, queryable live or statically, and the dashboard is built on the same public API.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is a huge like really comprehensive set of events that are emitted like as the session is streaming

takeaways.technique: Hill-climb skill for iterative prompt optimization
takeaways.what_they_do: A reusable skill that takes a prompt plus an objective and iteratively generates variants, optionally asking a human to pick a preferred output, grinding toward a better prompt; also used to distill a working manual process into an encoded skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claude API hill climb this prompt, and then it will work with you to iteratively like figure out, okay, what are we optimizing for
